title: Treated wastewater reuse remains limited and unevenly enabled

rootCauses.cause: JICA's preparatory report links the low reuse share to effluent quality at plants without tertiary treatment, but its underlying citation is ONAS (2021), which was not independently opened here. The evidence establishes a reported technical constraint, not its causal contribution to the national reuse share (SRC-TG-558).

Reuse also depends on conveyance and matching treated-water locations with uses: the parliamentary committee report records a statement that 42% of treated water was in Greater Tunis and that transfer lines were needed to facilitate its use. The report does not quantify how much this spatial constraint reduces reuse (SRC-TG-559).

JICA's report presents 125 plants, 28 with tertiary treatment and about 21% recycled; the 21% combines environmental protection, agriculture and irrigation and is not an irrigation-only rate.

The 2024 parliamentary committee report records ONAS's review of achievements to end-2023 and calls 57 and 293 million m3 annual volumes, but does not provide an independently auditable series. The 57/293 ratio should not be treated as a verified reuse rate or as directly comparable with the 2021 approximately 21% figure until definitions and periods are confirmed.

The committee report records the statement that 42% of treated water is in Greater Tunis and that transfer lines are needed; the speaker's office is not identifiable from the cited pages, and the geographical denominator, measurement year and underlying distribution series are not supplied.

The committee records a 2 July 2022 inter-ministerial circular formalising agricultural reuse. Its existence indicates a policy framework, but the evidence reviewed does not quantify implementation, compliance, uptake or water-quality outcomes.

No verified national measurement was located for actual agricultural reuse or uptake by irrigation perimeters such as Borj Touil. The World Bank describes millions of cubic metres made available to about 500 farmers and reports three demonstration plots irrigated with treated wastewater, not uptake volume (SRC-TG-556).
author: TahaGHZ
excerpt: The national sector report gives actual irrigation use and area for 2023/24. These figures are narrower than national all-purpose reuse. Treated wastewater reuse in Tunisia remains limited in the available national…

sections.heading: Problem
sections.content:
The national sector report gives actual irrigation use and area for 2023/24 (SRC-TG-530). These figures are narrower than national all-purpose reuse.

Treated wastewater reuse in Tunisia remains limited in the available national evidence, while reported infrastructure and location constraints affect whether effluent can be reused. JICA's 2023 preparatory report, citing ONAS (2021), states that 28 of 125 ONAS plants had tertiary treatment and about 21% of treated wastewater was recycled for environmental protection, agriculture and irrigation; it says most was discharged to rivers and other water bodies (SRC-TG-558). In 2024, ONAS officials told a parliamentary committee that their review of achievements to end-2023 recorded 293 million m3 treated and 57 million m3 reused annually, with the figures tied to that end-2023 review (SRC-TG-559). The 2021 and committee figures are distinct reported series and do not establish a trend or a verified agricultural reuse rate.

sections.heading: Root causes
sections.content: JICA's report links the low reuse share to lower effluent quality at plants without tertiary treatment; this is the report's explanation based on ONAS (2021), not an independently established causal estimate (SRC-TG-558). Reuse also requires conveyance to users: the committee report records a statement that 42% of treated water was located in Greater Tunis and transfer lines were needed to facilitate its use (SRC-TG-559). The source does not quantify the effect of either constraint. The committee report also records a statement that agricultural reuse had been formalised from 2 July 2022 through a joint circular of the environment, agriculture and health ministries; the evidence here does not establish how fully it was implemented (SRC-TG-559).

sections.heading: Evidence
sections.content:
JICA's December 2023 preparatory report gives national figures attributed to ONAS (2021): 125 operating plants, 28 equipped with tertiary treatment, and about 21% of treated wastewater recycled for environmental protection, agriculture and irrigation. The report links lower effluent quality at non-tertiary plants to the reported reuse share, but the underlying ONAS dataset was not separately opened (SRC-TG-558). In the 2024 committee report, the acting ONAS director general's end-2023 review gives separate annual volumes of 293 million m3 treated and 57 million m3 reused. These are officials' statements recorded in a parliamentary report, not an audited statistical series, and they are tied to the review of achievements to end-2023 (SRC-TG-559). The 42% Greater Tunis figure and call for transfer lines are likewise reported statements; the passage supplies no denominator definition or measurement year (SRC-TG-559).

For the Northern Tunis project, the World Bank says flow regulation at the El Hissiene basin made millions of cubic metres of recycled water available to about 500 farmers in Borj Touil, and reports that plots of three farmers were irrigated with treated wastewater. This project-level account documents availability and demonstration use, not total farmer uptake or a national reuse volume (SRC-TG-556).

sections.heading: Why confidence is what it is
sections.content: Confidence is medium. JICA's institutional report and the parliamentary committee report support the existence and scale of a reuse constraint, and identify technical and conveyance issues. The national figures are reported through secondary institutional documents: the underlying ONAS (2021) data were not separately inspected, while the 2024 volumes and spatial share are statements recorded in committee proceedings. Their definitions are incomplete and the 2021 and end-2023 reference periods differ. World Bank project reporting is useful for the Northern Tunis case but does not measure actual uptake at scale. No comparable, independently verified series establishes a trend or agricultural reuse rate.

sections.heading: Links to other sectors
sections.content: Reuse could provide irrigation water and potentially substitute for freshwater where quality, conveyance and monitoring permit. The sources document mixed-use national recycling and project-level availability and demonstration plots, but do not quantify freshwater displaced or total agricultural uptake (SRC-TG-556, SRC-TG-558, SRC-TG-559).

sections.heading: Leads for phase 2
sections.content:
- ONAS tertiary-treatment upgrades and wastewater-reuse programmes (SRC-TG-559).
- Northern Tunis wastewater storage, flow regulation and conveyance project (SRC-TG-556).

sections.heading: Verification
sections.content:
The national water report records about 11.3 million m³ reused for irrigation from 295 million m³ treated and 2,778 ha actually irrigated in 2023/24. The larger all-purpose reuse figures refer to different uses and cannot be substituted. Sources: SRC-TG-530 and SRC-TG-559.

**Independent review, 21 November 2026:** pass after corrections. Checked against the originals: RNE 2024 (SRC-TG-530) Tables VI.5 and VI.6 and the reuse text; JICA December 2023 (SRC-TG-558) national background section; the parliamentary committee report on bill 30/2024 (SRC-TG-559) pp. 7, 9 and 11; the World Bank Northern Tunis feature, 30 August 2022 (SRC-TG-556). Corrections: the 57 and 293 million m3 figures are now dated to the review of achievements to end-2023 as the source states (the "reference year unspecified" wording is removed from the indicators, `data_gaps`, body); the 42% statement and the 2 July 2022 circular are no longer attributed to named office-holders because the cited pages do not name the speakers. Independent teammate sign-off is outstanding; reviewer and author share the TahaGHZ identity, so the record is not validated.

resolvedSources.title: Rapport national du secteur de l'eau, année 2024
resolvedSources.publisher: Ministère de l'Agriculture, des Ressources Hydrauliques et de la Pêche (MARHP), Bureau de la Planification et des Equilibres Hydrauliques; hosted by ONAGRI
resolvedSources.extracts:
Synthèse générale, printed page 7:

> Au niveau de la demande, les quotas de l'irrigation ont été fortement réduits pour assurer la pérennité de l'arboriculture. Le volume consommé à partir des barrages est passé de 88,4 Mm3 en 2022-2023 à 46,7 Mm3 en 2023-2024.

> En bref, les mesures prises face au manque d'eau ont pu assurer l'approvisionnement en eau potable, mais l'agriculture irriguée a été clairement affectée.

> Les périmètres irrigués à partir des barrages n'ont pu bénéficier que de quantités minimes insuffisantes même au maintien de l'arboriculture. Les PPI irrigués à partir de Sidi Salem n'ont pu bénéficier que de 12 Mm3 pour des besoins dépassant les 100 millions.

> Les PPI de Nebhana spécialisés dans les cultures primeurs maraichères sous serre n'ont pu bénéficier d'eau d'irrigation et se sont trouvés en arrêt total avec toutes les conséquences négatives qui en résultent : baisse de la production nationale et montée des prix, pas de revenus des agriculteurs, terres délaissées et vouées aux extensions de l'urbanisme, GDA en chômage, ...

> Par ailleurs, le secteur irrigué s'est basé sur les ressources souterraines ce qui contribue à la croissance de leur surexploitation et la dégradation de leur qualité.

> Ce secteur rencontre des limites en termes d'intensification avec un taux global moyen de l'ordre de 90% mais très variable d'un périmètre à un autre en fonction de la situation du contexte socioéconomique.

English gloss (last sentence): The sector faces limits on intensification, with an overall average rate of about 90% but very variable from one perimeter to another.

English gloss: Irrigation quotas were cut sharply to keep orchards alive; consumption from dams fell from 88.4 Mm3 (2022-23) to 46.7 Mm3 (2023-24). Drinking water was secured but irrigated agriculture was "clearly affected". Dam-fed perimeters got minimal volumes, insufficient even for orchards; Sidi Salem PPIs got 12 Mm3 against needs above 100 Mm3. Nebhana PPIs, specialised in greenhouse early vegetables, got no irrigation water and stopped entirely: lower national output and higher prices, no farmer income, land abandoned to urban sprawl, GDAs idle. The irrigated sector fell back on groundwater, worsening overexploitation and quality.

Section II.1 "Restrictions d'usages" (irrigation), printed page 39:

> Le MARHP a notifié aux CRDAs de ne pas programmer les cultures d'été et les cultures consommatrices d'eau telles que les cucurbitacées et les légumes, et de limiter aux arbres fruitiers et aux cultures stratégiques (fourrages, betteraves sucrières et grandes cultures) dans les limites des quotas qui seront alloués aux périmètres irrigués liés aux barrages. Le volume consommé total à partir des barrages est passé de 88,4 Mm3 en 2022-2023 à 46,7 Mm3 en 2023-2024 (source : DGGREE),

> Le volume exploité à partir du système Mellègue-Bouhertma a été de l'ordre de 22 Mm3 contre 51 Mm3 l'année précédente (source : DGGREE),

> Malgré la faiblesse du quota alloué aux CRDA à partir du barrage Sidi Salem en 2023-2024 qui était de 22 Mm3, les CRDA n'ont pu bénéficier que de 12 Mm3. Le pompage illicite de l'eau lâchée à la Medjerda à partir de Sidi Salem pour atteindre les périmètres irrigués est parmi les causes essentielles de l'indisponibilité réelle du quota,

> La SECADENORD a facturé un volume total de 13 Mm3 aux CRDA en 2024 contre 23 en 2023 et 50 en 2022 (source : SECADENORD).

English gloss: The ministry told CRDAs not to plan summer crops or water-hungry crops (cucurbits, vegetables) and to limit irrigation from dams to fruit trees and "strategic" crops (fodder, sugar beet, field crops) within quotas. Total consumption from dams: 88.4 Mm3 (2022-23) to 46.7 Mm3 (2023-24). Mellègue-Bouhertma: 22 Mm3 against 51 Mm3 the year before. Sidi Salem quota for 2023-24 was 22 Mm3 but CRDAs received only 12 Mm3, mainly because of illicit pumping of the water released into the Medjerda. SECADENORD billed CRDAs 13 Mm3 in 2024, 23 in 2023, 50 in 2022.

Printed page 43:

> En irrigation, le système de quotas est encore plus sévère en 2024. Les volumes exploités à partir des barrages sont pratiquement réduits à moitié par rapport à 2023.

English gloss: In 2024 the irrigation quota system was even more severe; volumes used from dams were nearly halved compared with 2023.

Section I.4 "L'économie de l'eau d'irrigation", printed pages 58-59:

> Le Programme National d'Economie de l'EAU en Irrigation PNEEI a permis d'équiper 428 500 ha en équipements d'économie d'eau à la parcelle sur 442 500 ha de PI.

> L'irrigation localisée est pratiquée sur 219 900 ha, l'aspersion est pratiquée sur 113 900 ha. Le gravitaire amélioré est appliqué pour l'irrigation de 94 700 ha. Les investissements pour l'équipement en économie d'eau ont atteint depuis le démarrage du PNEE en 1995 jusqu'à 2024 le montant de 1709 MDT y compris les subventions.

English gloss: PNEEI has equipped 428,500 of 442,500 ha of irrigated perimeters (96.9%): drip 219,900 ha, sprinkler 113,900 ha, improved gravity 94,700 ha. Investment 1995-2024: 1,709 MTND including subsidies.

Conclusions, printed page 81:

> Quant à l'agriculture irriguée, les conditions hydriques défavorables ont causé certaines régressions sur la production des fruits et cultures maraichères. Les PPI de Nebhana n'ont pu bénéficier d'eau d'irrigation alors que les quotas alloués à ceux de la Basse Vallée de la Medjerda ont été très faibles.

English gloss: Unfavourable water conditions reduced fruit and vegetable production; Nebhana PPIs received no irrigation water and lower Medjerda PPIs very low quotas.
resolvedSources.notes:
- Opened via: curl + pdftotext (layout); saw: full text (184 pages). Latin-1 encoded; converted with iconv.
- Data year 2024 (irrigation campaign 2023-24); publication year 2025 inferred from press coverage of the "rapport 2024" in October 2025 (not opened as a source).
- The report gives no production figures by crop for 2023-24 in the passages read; effects are described qualitatively.
- 88.4 Mm3 (2022-23 consumption from all dams) and the 2023 report's Table 8 (Sidi Salem 18.7, Nebhana 4, Siliana group 4.8) are consistent in scale, but the 2023 report does not give an all-dam total.

resolvedSources.title: Tunisia: Recycled Wastewater Cleans Up the Sea, Provides Water for Farming
resolvedSources.extracts:
> 96% of a batch of samples of seawater collected at Raoued in 2020 complied with levels of bacteria considered safe for public health; 97% for the level of detergents. These improvements were the result of channeling treated wastewater underground through pipes to a submarine outfall—the technical term for a pipeline under the sea—stretching 6 kilometers offshore before discharging its effluent 20 meters down the surface.

> A poorly maintained, 30-year-old sewage system that was in place could no longer cope with the volume of waste being generated. Open and above ground, its channels carried wastewater from the Chotrana treatment plant, just south of Raoued, to the El Khelij river, discharging it as the river hit the beach. [...] Even though it was treated, the quality of the wastewater was too poor for agriculture.

> The improvements are the result of a US$60.6 million project that was completed in 2021.

> From the basin, its flow can be regulated for irrigation, making millions of cubic meters of good quality, recycled water available to about 500 farmers in Borj Touil.

> To show the public that recycled wastewater is safe for growing plants, plots belonging to three farmers in Borj Touil have been irrigated with treated wastewater
resolvedSources.notes:
- Opened via: curl of the HTML page, text extracted; saw: full text.
- Promotional feature by the lender of the project; it reports water "made available" to Borj Touil farmers, not volumes actually used. Treat claims of success with care; no uptake figure is given.

resolvedSources.title: Rapport de l'étude préparatoire pour le projet de construction d'une station avancée de traitement des eaux usées à Gabès en République tunisienne
resolvedSources.publisher: Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) for ONAS
resolvedSources.extracts:
Chapter 1, project background (PDF page 30):

> Dans ce contexte, le gouvernement tunisien a fixé l'objectif de réutiliser 50% ou plus des eaux usées épurées dans son Plan quinquennal de développement national (2016-2020) et a identifié la promotion de l'utilisation des eaux usées épurées comme une priorité dans le Plan de développement du secteur de l'assainissement « Réutilisation des eaux usées 2050 » en cours d'élaboration.

> Actuellement, 125 stations d'épuration sont en place dans les circonscriptions administratives et les régions de plus de 3 000 habitants relevant de l'Office National de l'Assainissement tunisien (ci-dessous repris « ONAS »). Cependant, seules 28 de ces stations sont équipées d'installations de traitement tertiaire telles que filtration et traitement par ultraviolets, et la qualité des eaux épurées dans les installations de traitement dépourvues d'équipements tertiaires n'est pas élevée, ce qui fait que seulement environ 21% du total des eaux usées épurées sont recyclées à des fins de protection de l'environnement, d'agriculture et d'irrigation, et la majorité rejetée dans les rivières et autres plans d'eau. (ONAS, 2021).

English gloss: The 2016-2020 five-year plan set a target of reusing 50% or more of treated wastewater. ONAS runs 125 plants; only 28 have tertiary treatment (filtration, UV). Effluent from plants without tertiary treatment is of low quality, so only about 21% of treated wastewater is recycled (environmental protection, agriculture, irrigation); most is discharged to rivers and other water bodies (ONAS, 2021).
resolvedSources.notes:
- Opened via: curl + pdftotext; saw: full text available (report dated December 2023); only the national background and environmental framework sections were read for this record.
- The 21% figure includes "environmental protection" uses, so it is not comparable with irrigation-only reuse rates.
- The rest of the report concerns the Gabès plant and industrial reuse by the Groupe Chimique Tunisien, which belongs to another research block (Gabès, 600-624).

resolvedSources.extracts:
Page 3, purpose of the bill:

> يهدف مشروع القانون المعروض إلى الموافقة على اتفاق الضمان عند أول طلب المُبرم بتاريخ 31 جانفي 2024 بين الجمهورية التونسية والبنك الافريقي للتنمية والمتعلق بالقرض المسند لفائدة الديوان الوطني للتطهير للمساهمة في تمويل مشروع تحسين جودة المياه المستعملة والمعالجة لدعم مجابهة التغيرات المناخية بمبلغ لا يتجاوز 81,9 مليون أورو أي ما يعادل حوالي 276,14 مليون دينار.

English gloss: The bill approves the State guarantee of a loan of up to EUR 81.9 million (about 276.14 million TND) from the African Development Bank to ONAS, signed 31 January 2024, to improve the quality of wastewater and treated water.

Page 3:

> سيساهم هذا المشروع عموما في دعم مردودية التطهير والتحكم في الطاقة من خلال تجديد المعدات الكهروميكانيكية واستخدام الطاقة الشمسية الفلطوضوئية في 19 محطة تطهير موزعة على 11 ولاية

> بفضل المعالجة الثلاثية للمياه المستعملة، سيساهم هذا المشروع في إنتاج مياه المعالجة مطابقة للمواصفات التونسية وإعادة استعمالها في المجال الفلاحي، حيث سينتفع أكثر من 3000 هكتار من الأراضي الزراعية المتواجدة بقرب محطات التطهير المعنية.

English gloss: The project will renew electromechanical equipment and install solar PV at 19 treatment plants in 11 governorates. Through tertiary treatment it will produce treated water that meets Tunisian standards for agricultural reuse, benefiting more than 3,000 ha near the plants.

Page 6, deputies' remarks:

> كما تعرّضوا الى إشكاليات نظام الصّرف الصحي في جل المناطق والذي يعاني سوء الصيانة مما تسبّب في عديد المخلّفات على غرار التلوث البيئي والروائح الكريهة والمخاطر على الصحة عموما.

> ولاحظ عديد النواب غياب التخطيط في مثل هذه المشاريع، وغياب أمثلة تهيئة عمرانية واضحة ونظرة استراتيجية لتطوير كيفية استغلال المياه المستعملة المعالجة.

English gloss: Deputies raised the poor maintenance of the sewer system in most areas, causing pollution, odours and health risks, and noted the lack of planning and of a strategic view on how to use treated wastewater.

Page 7, presentation by the acting director general of ONAS:

> واستعرض إنجازات القطاع إلى موفى سنة 2023 والمتمثلة خاصة في تبني 197 بلديّة ( 9,24 مليون ساكنا) وانتفاع حوالي 7,29 مليون ساكنا مرتبطين بالشبكة بالمدن المتبنّاة وإنجاز 18243كلم من القنوات و122 محطة تطهير كما تمت معالجة 293 مليون متر مكعب من المياه المعالجة سنويًا ويتم إعادة استعمال 57 مليون متر مكعب من المياه المعالجة سنويًا.

English gloss: Sector status at end-2023: 197 municipalities taken over by ONAS (9.24 million inhabitants), about 7.29 million people connected, 18,243 km of sewers and 122 treatment plants; 293 million m3 treated per year, of which 57 million m3 per year is reused.

Page 7, ONAS strategy, axis 2:

> تحسين نوعية المياه المعالجة قصد تنمية إعادة استعمالها في مختلف المجالات التنموية من خلال تهذيب وتوسعة محطات التطهير المتقادمة وتركيز المعالجة الثلاثية وفصل المياه الصناعية عن المياه الحضرية.

English gloss: Improve treated-water quality to develop its reuse, by upgrading and extending ageing treatment plants, installing tertiary treatment, and separating industrial from urban wastewater.

Page 8:

> وكذلك مشروع اللّزمة (قسط تونس الكبرى) وتأهيل محطّة التطهير شطرانة 2 وتجهيزها بمعالجة ثلاثيّة.

English gloss: The Greater Tunis concession project includes rehabilitating the Choutrana 2 plant and equipping it with tertiary treatment.

Page 9, Secretary of State for water:

> كما أوضح أن 42 % من المياه المعالجة موجودة في تونس الكبرى ويجب إنشاء خطوط تحويل لتسهيل استعمال هذه المياه

English gloss: 42% of treated water is in Greater Tunis, and transfer lines must be built to make it usable.

Page 11, Minister of Environment's reply:

> وأفادت أن ملف إعادة استعمال المياه المستعملة في المجال الفلاحي تم تكريسه منذ 2 جويلية 2022 بعد صدور منشور مشترك بين الوزارات المكلفة بالبيئة والفلاحة والصحة في الغرض مشيرة إلى التجربة التونسية رغم ضعف الموارد البشرية.

English gloss: Agricultural reuse was formalised from 2 July 2022 by a joint circular of the ministries of environment, agriculture and health, despite weak human resources.
resolvedSources.notes:
- Opened via: curl; the PDF's text layer drops Arabic letters (only digits survive), so the 12 pages were rendered with PyMuPDF and read visually. Extracts are transcribed from the page images. Saw: full text (12 pages).
- Figures are statements by officials (ONAS, ministries) to a parliamentary committee, recorded in its report; they are not audited statistics. The 293/57 Mm3 figures are given as annual values in a review of achievements "to end-2023", without a stated reference year.
- Committee sessions were held on 8 May 2024 and in early July 2024 (page 2 says 3 July, page 6 says 4 July for the hearing of the ministers and ONAS).
